## Multivariate panel data

MTRClust expects a numeric `n x T x p` array. The first dimension indexes
units, the second indexes ordered time points, and the third indexes variables.

## Robust clustering problem

The method estimates smooth low-rank cluster trajectories while trimming a
prespecified fraction of units and recording multilevel outlier diagnostics.

## MTRClust overview

The algorithm robustly scales variables, initializes candidate partitions,
alternates assignment and smooth low-rank center updates, and returns the best
valid candidate according to the objective.

## Input preparation

```{r}
library(MTRClust)
dat <- simulate_mtr_panel(n = 30, tt = 15, p = 3, seed = 11)
dim(dat$x)
```

## Fitting

```{r}
fit <- mtrclust(dat$x, k = 3, alpha = 0.05, rank = 2,
                nstart = 2, max_iter = 20, seed = 11)
fit
```

## Interpreting clusters and trimming

```{r}
summary(fit)
head(mtrclust_diagnostics(fit, type = "units"))
```

## Interpreting termination and rollback

`fit$termination` records why the iteration stopped. `fit$converged` records
whether the numerical convergence conditions were met. `fit$rolled_back`
records whether a nonconverged candidate was restored to its best objective
iterate.

## Multilevel outlier diagnostics

```{r}
mtrclust_diagnostics(fit)
```

Observation outliers, global sensor-time faults, temporal points, multivariate
segments, sensor segments, isolated cells, and raw candidate detections are
reported separately. They should not be summed as independent events.

## Visualization

```{r}
plot(fit, type = "objective")
plot(fit, type = "sizes")
```

## Reproducibility

Use the `seed` argument for deterministic sequential runs. Parallel execution is
not exported in this checkpoint because reproducible parallel RNG behavior has
not yet been validated.

## Current limitations

The package currently requires complete finite numeric arrays, does not impute
missing data, and uses the audited sequential prototype algorithm without
performance-oriented rewrites.
